expected_evidence: Geological: sediment/lake-core stratigraphy (e.g., Lake Agassiz outflow channels, Gulf of Mexico/St. Lawrence estuary cores) showing a freshwater-pulse signature (oxygen-isotope excursions, meltwater-sensitive foraminifera) time-correlated with the onset of Younger Dryas cooling across multiple sites/continents.

Geological: absence or mistiming of purported impact-winter markers (platinum anomaly, nanodiamonds, magnetic/glass spherules, soot/charcoal spikes) relative to the actual cooling onset, or demonstration that such markers are geographically limited/non-synchronous rather than global.

Astronomical/cosmogenic: lack of independent extraterrestrial signatures (no matching cosmic-impact ejecta layer, no crater evidence) needed to support an impact-driven biomass-burning winter, and ice-core records (e.g., GISP2/GRIP) showing forcing patterns inconsistent with a single continent-spanning airburst.

Material/archaeological: charcoal and macro-charcoal records testing whether continent-wide biomass burning actually preceded or coincided with cooling, and 'black mat' site stratigraphy re-interpreted as local wildfire rather than global impact winter.
Genetic: megafaunal ancient-DNA population-decline timing used to argue extinction was gradual (consistent with climate/meltwater forcing) rather than an abrupt impact-driven collapse.

Model-prior (paleoclimate literature): published multi-site replication studies/meta-analyses concluding Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis markers are not reproducible or global, reinforcing meltwater-forcing as the dominant mechanism.
response.rationale: This is fundamentally a paleoclimate-proxy debate rather than a human-witnessed or textually recorded event, so textual/linguistic/oral-tradition/iconographic channels are essentially inapplicable (rightly near-zero in the table) and their absence carries no evidential weight against the hypothesis. The mechanism in question (meltwater pulse vs. impact-winter/biomass-burning) is adjudicated almost entirely through geological archives (varved lake sediments, marine/lake cores, ice cores) and cosmogenic/astronomical marker layers, both of which have comparatively high younger-dryas detectability (geological 0.65, astronomical 0.7) because these media are physically robust, widely sampled, and are in fact the actual battleground of the real Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis controversy. (model-prior, unverified: this reflects an actual ongoing scientific debate — Firestone et al. 2007 impact hypothesis vs. the mainstream meltwater-forcing view — where multiple replication studies have failed to confirm impact markers at many sites, lending some real-world plausibility to a 'refuted' framing, though the debate is not universally settled). Material (charcoal, archaeological black-mat sites, 0.35) and genetic (megafaunal DNA timing, 0.3) evidence are moderately preserved but noisier and more locally variable, contributing weaker, more equivocal signal. Given that the core evidentiary channels (geological, astronomical/cosmogenic) are well-preserved and have in fact been extensively sampled in the real literature, an absence of confirmed impact markers is genuinely informative rather than merely an artifact of poor preservation — supporting a moderate-to-good overall detectability (~0.5) for this hypothesis, dominated by the strong geological/astronomical channels but pulled down by the weak textual/oral/iconographic and moderate material/genetic channels.
